_comment: R8.2 -- the authored stronghold route. MEADOWS_PROGRESSION_SPEC.md Sec8 names exactly five spaces in exactly one order (Outer Works -> Courtyard / Hall Approach -> Tether Chamber Approach -> Warden Arena -> Legendary Chamber) with a 30-60 minute first-clear target, and rules out a giant puzzle dungeon in the same breath. So this is a COMPACT authored route: five rooms on one L-shaped spine, no branches, no keys to hunt, one door. Everything that is a number, a position or a species lives here; scripts/world/stronghold.gd is only the machine that stands it up. ALL NUMBERS TUNABLE per CLAUDE.md.
_comment_where: T1-HALL (2026-08-30), owner directive: the castle IS the Meadows Hall IS the stronghold -- one location, not the works behind a separate castle 154m away. `ralph/reports/HALL_DESIGN_2026-08-30.md` is the design this re-site and the massing in `stronghold.gd::_build_hall_massing()` both answer; its §2 has the re-derived bearing and the probe evidence, its §9 the implementation order. `scripts/world/landmark.gd`'s detached castle at (150,7595) retires (its own `SITE`/history stay in the file as a record; `playground_world.gd` stops calling it) -- nothing stands there any more. The five chambers' own local `at`/`size` values below are UNCHANGED by this merge; only `site.at`/`yaw_deg`/`ramp_run` moved (see `_comment_ow5d_relocation` below for the re-derivation) and a new massing layer stands on top of the same route. Original siting evidence, still true of the chambers' own internal layout: `tools/_probe_stronghold.gd` sampled an 8m grid over the pre-corridor map and found (1) the terrain ends past a certain range, ruling out a deep-east layout, (2) a rise climbs sharply west of a deep-west layout, which no flat floor can sit above, (3) the band this layout uses has 6.4m of relief and no gaps. Every chamber corner falls outside `world_perimeter.gd`'s boundary ring; how the player is let onto this ground is `SF34`'s three-Sigil approach gate, not this file's business.
_comment_frame: T1-HALL (2026-08-30): `site.yaw_deg` moved 90 -> 0 (see `_comment_ow5d_relocation`), so this note is rewritten rather than merely re-read. `site.at` is the OUTER WORKS' own centre in world metres, and `site.yaw_deg` 0 leaves the complex's LOCAL frame identical to WORLD: local +z (the route's depth axis) IS world +z, so walking deeper walks SOUTH, matching the corridor's own approach from the north. Local +x is world +x. Chamber `at` is [lateral, depth] in that local frame and `size` is [lateral width, depth]. Chambers joined by a passage MUST share the perpendicular axis exactly (the wall opener splits one wall at its own centre; it does not cut diagonals) -- the L's corner is handled by the arena and the chamber sharing its depth, not by an offset.
_comment_ow5d_relocation: OW5D moved `site.at` to (0,7560) with `yaw_deg` left at 90 UNCHANGED and flagged loudly as 'very likely WRONG' -- nobody had re-probed the ground or re-derived the approach bearing. T1-HALL (2026-08-30) does both, per `HALL_DESIGN_2026-08-30.md` §2: `tools/_probe_hall_site.gd` sampled an 8m grid over x[-72,40] z[7490,7682] against the LIVE heightfield (superseding the un-probed OW5D placeholder). Findings: the player arrives through a low bowl (trail at -6.9 around (20,7480), rising to -0.65 at the old terminus); a local rise peaks +4.8 around (8-16,7586-7602) -- inside the courtyard footprint, so the building genuinely sits on a hill; a western shoulder climbs to +7..+9 at x[-72,-40] to lean the keep against; a ravine drops to -8..-16 just north-west of the causeway, dressed rather than fought. `site.at` moved 8m east, to (8.0,7560.0), so the western shoulder's high ground (+5.6..+6.8) sits clear of the legendary chamber rather than under it, leaving the courtyard rise (+4.8) as the binding high point. `yaw_deg` moves 90 -> 0: local +z (route depth) now maps to world +z, so walking deeper walks SOUTH and the mouth (outer_works' own -z face) faces NORTH -- straight up the corridor the player actually arrives along, matching the trail's final leg (20,7480)->(0,7560) instead of standing side-on to it. This is a real cost, not a free win: `art.json`'s `sun.yaw_deg` is 140 (south sky), so the re-derived north-facing gate is a SHADED face at the day keyframe -- HALL_DESIGN_2026-08-30.md §2/§5/§6 own that deliberately (light stone tier + the proven fire/sky-fill recipe + self-lit occupation concentrated on this face; the sunlit flanks carry the coursing evidence instead). `ramp_run` moves 26 -> 40: mouth sill at floor +5.5, ramp-foot ground at (8,7508) ~ -4.8, so ~10.3m of rise over 40m is ~14.5 degrees, a real climb comfortably under the walkable bar (`_build_approach_ramp` self-derives the rise from the ground; only the run is authored). Everything already aimed at (0,7560) keeps working: the 15-pylon line ends at (-8,7505), 55m short of the new mouth and now pointing at the west half of the works, which is where the legendary chamber and the machine actually stand. The Sigil Gate, the waystop and the Band 5 trail need no edits. T1-HALL ALSO FOUND AND FIXED a real regression this re-site exposed but did not cause: `stronghold.gd::_place_gauntlet()` and `stronghold_climax.gd::_place_warden()` apply `facing_deg` directly as a WORLD angle to trainers parented to the world root (unlike every other placement in this file, which composes with the site's own rotation via `to_global`/parent-child transform) -- so a gauntlet trainer's or the Warden's facing did NOT rotate with the building when `yaw_deg` changed, and the resulting mismatch between a trainer's facing and its own room's new orientation was enough, in the tightest two rooms on the route, to push a fight's engagement geometry outside the footprint `built_floor_height_at()` recognises as this building's floor. See those two functions' own comments for the fix and `built_floor_height_at()` below for the margin this pass widened to keep the fix robust to the combat system's own multi-round placement drift, which is pre-existing and outside this file's ownership.
_comment_value_drop_t1_hall_4: T1-HALL-4, 2026-08-30, JUDGE-6 defect 1. The works' own exterior half of the value drop described in building_prefabs.json's `_why_value_drop_t1_hall_4` -- read that first, it carries the measurement and the reasoning. `stone_light` #9c9083 -> #5f5e58 and `stone_skirt` #8f8172 -> #575147 are the SAME factor the kit's LightRock/DarkRock take, applied here so the ladder HALL_DESIGN sec5 authored and `_comment_stone_light`/`_comment_stone_skirt` below both describe survives the drop intact: skirt < works walls < DarkRock < LightRock is unchanged in order, and the works-to-LightRock step stays 1.36x where it was 1.35x. What moves is the family's absolute value, because JUDGE-6 measured the fortress at five luminance points off its own background and the reference at a 32-point separation with the fortress dark. `stone` (#6a6157) is DELIBERATELY NOT DROPPED and that is not an oversight. `_wall_material` hands `stone_light` to outer walls and `stone` to inner ones, so `stone` is an interior tone, and `_ceiling_colour`'s own note records what happened the last time this building's interiors lost value: the warden arena went to 96.7% of pixels below luminance 40 and a blind critic's first finding was the value crush. The exterior is now slightly darker than the interior, which is both the intended read (a weathered outside, lit rooms within) and the only way to take the silhouette without paying for it in the five rooms the player fights in.
_comment_stone_light: T1-HALL-BUILD (2026-08-30), HALL_DESIGN_2026-08-30.md §5's palette-proof step: `stone_light` (the works' own exterior wall / exterior-face-skin tone, `stronghold.gd::_stone_light`/`_exterior_face_material`) moves from the code default #786d5e to the design's #9c9083, so the works' true exterior wears the SAME value-ladder step as the castle kit's retuned walls -- 'one stone, one scale, one value ladder, both kits'. `stone`/`stone_dark`/`floor_colour` are interior tones this pass does not touch; nothing else in `site` changed.
_comment_stone_skirt: T1-HALL-REBUILD (2026-08-30), HALL_DESIGN_2026-08-30.md §5's foundation tier -- the darkest step on the ladder (skirt < works walls < DarkRock < LightRock < coping), at the coarser 0.22 tile so the foundation reads as BIGGER blocks than the wall above it. It is worn by a facing skin (`stronghold.gd::_build_skirt_facing`), not by the skirt slab itself: each chamber's floor slab IS its skirt (one box 18m deep whose top face is the room's walkable floor), so retinting the slab would repaint five interiors. Before this the building's whole visible plinth rendered as yard cobble seen edge-on, at a smaller stone scale than the wall standing on it -- the exact scale collision §5 resolves with a stated ladder.
_comment_approach_pylons: BAND5-CONTENT, prompt 66. Three of that prompt's asks are one object, so they are built once rather than three times: the `navigation spine` ("pylons/landmarks should create readable world-space direction without becoming magical GPS"), `pylon/tether machinery readability`, and the environmental storytelling clause ("use existing machinery ... rather than inventing unrelated lore"). Band 5 had NONE of it. The chapter's conduit network stopped at the relay (z 3749) and the quarry (z 1790) and the last 680m -- the approach to the thing the whole network feeds -- was open meadow with a castle on the horizon. The run is the answer: an unbroken, LIT trunk line arriving at the works, the exact opposite statement to the seven spokes' broken-and-dead runs, and the same one `old_quarry.json`'s own `_comment_pylons` already makes (D41: present-tense machinery doing present-tense harm, not ruins).
_comment_approach_pylons_why_a_line: Why a straight line beside a wandering road, and not pylons ON the road. The trail's own Band 5 waypoints swing +-80m either side of x=0 (terrain_playground.json `trail.bands`), which is what stops the region being a corridor. A line that followed it would be a handrail -- literally magical GPS in world geometry, the thing the prompt names. A STRAIGHT line the road keeps crossing is the opposite: it is a BEARING. The player loses sight of it around every rise, meets it again, and each time it is pointing the same way. Direction comes from the line's own convergence in perspective, which is free and needs no marker, no minimap and no objective arrow.
_comment_approach_pylons_measured: SITED BY MEASUREMENT, not by guess -- `tools/_probe_band5_pylon_line.gd`, which exists to answer the one question a config cannot: `severed_spokes.gd::_conduit_span` sags the cable `distance * 0.05` below an attachment at `height * 0.66` computed from EACH pylon's OWN base, so ground rising between two stations pushes itself up into a cable derived from the two ends. The first candidate (13 stations, 9m) put the cable 1.74m over the ground on span 4->5 -- head height on a 1.8m player, a defect that shows only in a render. The probe swept height against station count: 15 stations at 10.0m is the SMALLEST height that clears comfortably, worst clearance 3.14m. Relief across the run is 11.77m (-3.46 to 8.31), which is why this had to be measured at all. Re-run the probe before moving any station.
_comment_approach_pylons_healing: This run needs no ending work and gets its payoff for free. `meadow_healing.json`'s `tether_lights` finds every LIT Team Tether fitting by WHAT ITS MATERIAL IS rather than by node name, precisely so the three files that build pylons all pay off together -- so all fifteen of these go dark on the walk home from the Warden, along with the quarry's four and the relay's. The last region to get the network is also the last to lose it, in the player's own line of sight.

approach_pylons._comment_round2:
Blind visual pass round 1 called the pylons "the best thing in the survey" and the wire between them "a bezier debug line, not a hanging cable -- cables sag, they do not soar", concluding "the wire connecting them undoes them." So the fix is the wire. `severed_spokes.gd::_conduit_span` sags a span by `distance * 0.05 * sag_scale`, and sag is PROPORTIONAL TO SPAN -- the default 1.0 was tuned on the spokes' and the quarry's ~14m spans, where it droops 0.7m and reads; over this run's 35m spans it droops 1.8m over five times the length, which is a straight diagonal. 2.2 takes it to 11% of span.

Sag and ground clearance pull directly against each other, so both were swept together rather than either being guessed (`tools/_sweep_cable.gd`): at the old 10.0m height, 2.2 puts the cable 1.01m off the ground -- under a walking player. 12.0m is the height that buys the sag back, and it is the SMALLEST of the swept heights that keeps a 2.2x sag clear of 2.2m (worst 2.33m). The cost is a pylon 20% taller than the one the critic liked, which is the trade taken deliberately: a decisive fix that round 2 can actually see, over a timid one that changes nothing.
approach_pylons._comment_height: ROUND 2: 10.0 -> 12.0, see `_comment_round2` -- the height is now set by the CABLE, not by the pylon. Original reasoning, still true: against the quarry spur run's 4.6m. This is the trunk that feeds the Hall and it should out-scale every spur the player has met; 10.0 is also the measured floor for cable clearance (see `_comment_approach_pylons_measured`) rather than a number picked for drama. `_build_pylons` scales the one GLB uniformly, so a 10m pylon is a 4.6m pylon at 2.17x -- heavier as well as taller, which is the correct read for a trunk.

abreast of Watchman Corr's outer watch (bands/band5_stronghold_approach/trainers.json order 5005, (-68,7140)) -- the first Team Tether body and the first Team Tether machinery in the same 40m, so the faction reads as one thing that both stands on this ground and takes from it.

the middle of the run and the middle of the region. The trail's own waypoint (80,7370) swings 100m EAST of here, so this is the stretch where the road and the line visibly diverge and the line is the one that keeps pointing at the Hall -- a bearing, not a handrail.

level with the three-Sigil gate's own latitude, z=7400. The gate itself sits at (63.6,7400) -- ON the road, after this lane moved it there (playground_world.gd SIGIL_GATE_AT) -- so the line passes 78m WEST of it. That separation is the point rather than an accident: the road's gate is the thing the player has to open, and the machinery runs past it untouched on its own bearing. Team Tether's power was never stopped by the door they make everybody else use.

in sight of `the_waystop` (props.json order 5001, (-25,7460)), 17.6m outside its 14m clearing. A player who stops at the last camp to sort their five looks up at the thing they are about to walk into. Deliberately just outside the clearing so it frames the camp rather than standing in it.
the last one before the works, 55.6m short of the outer works' centre and clear of the skirt. The run does not stop -- it arrives.

_comment_approach_drain: BAND5-CONTENT, prompt 66's environmental storytelling clause. The full reasoning, and an honest statement of the half of the effect this does NOT own, is in `scripts/world/approach_drain_skin.gd`'s header. The short version: `terrain_playground.json`'s `drains.stations` holds seven entries, four at the quarry (z~1790) and three at the relay (z~3749), and NONE in Band 5 -- so the drained ground got weaker the closer the player walked to the machine draining it. `bounds` is the corridor the fifteen `approach_pylons` run through, with margin; the skin's alpha is `playground_heightfield.drain_factor()` itself, so it paints exactly where a station says and NOTHING anywhere else. It therefore renders nothing today and says so in the build log: `drains.stations` is a file no Gate D lane may edit (GATE_D_LANE_CONTRACT §5), so the Band 5 stations are REQUESTED in this lane's report the same way a `density_scale` is, and this is shipped ahead of them so that granting the request is one edit to one data file rather than an edit plus a code change.

approach_drain._comment_bounds: [min_x, min_z, max_x, max_z]. Wraps the pylon run (x -40 -> -8 over z 7010 -> 7505) with roughly 22m of margin west and east, which carries the widest station radius the request asks for without sampling ground the drain can never reach. Cell 4.0 against the relay skin's 3.0 because this corridor is 540m long rather than 92m across and the alpha gradient here is broad -- a finer cell would multiply quads to no visible end. T1-HALL (2026-08-30), design §6.6: max_z extended 7530 -> 7548 (the outer_works front wall's own world z, post re-site) so the drained-ground skin reaches the building that is doing the draining, instead of stopping 18m short of it.
approach_drain._comment_tint: `terrain_playground.json`'s own `drains.tint`, not a new colour, so the runtime skin and the eventual bake agree. That file's `_comment_tint` explains why it sits close to the healthy near-white: the colour map MULTIPLIES the PBR albedo, and a darker tint here would be a brightness change pretending to be a colour.

_comment_language: R8.2's brief: a sacred natural site INDUSTRIALISED by Tether. The same grammar `SE23` uses at the relay, at full scale here. In geometry that means three things and nothing more elaborate: the shell is old cut stone (`site.stone`, the same weathered value family the castle's own plinth uses), every space carries Team Tether hardware bolted ONTO that stone rather than replacing it (`trim` bands and `conduits` below, in the reserved oxblood and the reserved teal from palette.json), and the deeper you go the more of the room is machine and the less of it is masonry. `conduits` are lit teal runs; they all point at the Legendary Chamber because that is where the power comes from, which is `SG40`'s reveal drawn a room early and never said out loud.
_comment_chambers: `open: true` means no roof -- the outer works and the courtyard are open-air yards inside high walls, the three inner spaces are roofed. `height` is floor-to-ceiling (or wall height, for the open ones). The Legendary Chamber's 22m is set by the machine, not by taste: the board draws it at ~15m against its own 0-20m scale bar, so the room has to be architecture-sized or the centrepiece cannot stand up in it.

Sec8: trainer fight, environmental storytelling. World box x[159.8,187.8] z[-226.4,-204.4].
Sec8: elite trainer, recovery opportunity. Roofed, and the first space that is more machine than masonry. World box x[196.8,214.8] z[-223.4,-207.4].

Sec8: tether mechanism, freeing sequence, voluntary join, release ceremony. Built AROUND the machine. World box x[218.0,246.0] z[-197.4,-169.4] -- directly behind the castle's own plinth (z[-154.4,-134.4]), 15m clear of it.

_comment_passages: One spine, in route order, no branches. `gated_by_flag` is the complex's ONE door: a Tether blast shutter across the way into the Warden Arena that lifts when the elite in front of it has been beaten. Deliberately NOT an `item_gate.gd` gate -- that class is a carried KEY operating the world, `SF34`'s three Sigils are the carried keys that open the Hall APPROACH from outside, and nothing in here hands out a key. 'You have beaten the thing standing in the doorway' is already a fact the SB9 flag store remembers across saves, which is the same call `burrow_warrens.gd` made for its vault door and for the same reason.
_comment_trim: Team Tether hardware bolted onto old stone. `band` is a horizontal girder run along one wall of a chamber at `y` above the floor; `pillar` is an upright brace at an `offset` from the chamber centre. Oxblood by default (`site.tether_trim`, palette.json's reserved faction colour); `lit: true` swaps to the reserved teal with emission, which marks a run that is CARRYING something.
_comment_interior_structure: CONTENT-0828B. Owner playtest 2026-08-28 sec4a: 'burrow warrens and the castle are the lame looking locations. basically everywhere we had to build an under ground or build a building.' He named a CLASS of space rather than two sites, so the answer is a shared method -- scripts/world/interior_structure.gd, which burrow_warrens.json consumes from the same file with a different vocabulary. That file's header carries the mechanism; the short version is that a chamber assembled from six flat boxes has exactly two scales of incident (the room, and its props) where the meadow outside has five or six, and the missing MIDDLE scale is why an interior reads as blockout however good its texture is. The five passes supply it: a vertical member at a repeating pitch along every wall (`bays`), a jointed band at mid-height (`course`), ceiling ribs landed on the same divisions so wall and roof read as one structure (`ribs`), a jamb-and-lintel frame around every cut opening (`reveals`), and a post in each internal corner (`corners`). None of it is solid, none of it enters a doorway, and none of it reaches further into a room than interior_structure.gd's MAX_PROJECT_M -- half the metre `combat_arena_bounds_at()` reserves from every wall, so the Warden fight keeps the arena it was tuned against. `enabled: false` turns the whole pass off. ALL TUNABLE.
_comment_interior_structure_castle: This building's VOCABULARY, against the cave's. `jitter: 0` is the difference in code: masonry lands on its pitch exactly, and any lean at all reads as a mistake rather than as rock. `bay_pitch_m` 3.6 against the cave's 2.9 -- these spaces are 16-28m across and up to 22m tall, and the cave's tighter pitch would crowd a hall. This does NOT replace `trim` above: those are Team Tether girders and conduit, faction hardware bolted onto the stone, and they say who occupies the building; this is the building. Roles take the castle's own three stone values via stronghold.gd::_structure_colour (`stone` for shafts and corners, `stone_light` for capitals and the course, `stone_dark` for ribs and reveals) so nothing here introduces a fourth stone -- add a `tints` block here to override any role. The value steps matter more than they look: every interior light in this complex sets shadow_enabled=false, so a member proud of a wall is lit almost exactly like the wall behind it and only the value separates them.

interior_structure._comment_ragged: Masonry: OFF. This is the key that separates the two vocabularies along with `jitter` -- the Warrens turns it on so its ribs die out like rock, and dressed stone in a fortress does not. See burrow_warrens.json's own `_comment_ragged`.
interior_structure._comment_corbel: A bracket under each end of every ceiling rib, so a beam is caught by the wall rather than driven through it. See burrow_warrens.json's `_comment_corbel` for the finding that put them there.

_comment_conduits: Lit teal cable runs along the floor, every one of them pointing deeper. `from`/`to` are chamber ids; the run is drawn between their centres at ankle height and is DECORATION ONLY (no collider) so it can never block a doorway or trip a fight.
_comment_lights: Not a cave. The two open yards are lit by the sky and get only a low fill; the roofed rooms get real Tether worklights, and the Legendary Chamber is lit mostly BY the machine (see `machine.core_light`). `at` is chamber-local [lateral, depth], `y` is above the floor.
_comment_lights_measured: CONTENT-0828B. Playtest 4a's own second named direction is 'lighting authored per space rather than inherited', and a blind critic measuring the round-3 frames put a number on what these two rooms had: C2-warden-arena is 97.2% below luminance 40 with no midtone population at all, so the WARDEN -- the chapter's boss -- renders as a roughly 25-pixel dark smudge on a dark wall, and C1's legendary spire, which has the best-authored silhouette in the set, loses the readability contest to the floor trim. Those are the two most important moments in the chapter and both were invisible. This is a measured response to a measured defect rather than a taste call: warden_arena 0.8 -> 1.45 energy and 20 -> 24 range, legendary_chamber 0.55 -> 1.05 and 24 -> 30. Colours are UNCHANGED -- the cool grey-blue is authored and this is not a mood change, it is putting a midtone under the value structure so a silhouette has something to read against. The other four lights are untouched; the outer works and the courtyard are open to the real sky and the tether approach is deliberately the dim one. NOT verified on device: frame cost of raising an omni's range is [OWNER-ONLY] and shadow_enabled stays false on all of them. ALL TUNABLE.
_comment_lights_exterior: T1-ARCH (2026-08-29), owner evidence 'the stronghold: bad'. `stronghold_occupation.gd` already diagnosed and fixed this exact failure mode for `landmark.gd`'s castle: `art.json` puts the sun in the north sky, every approach here is on the south side (`_build_approach_ramp` exits toward decreasing local z), so the hero face is backlit at every hour the chapter is played -- and that file's own header says outright that the stronghold route built here 'is a different building entirely... untouched by it'. `shots/t1arch/S-ext-01-approach-ramp-foot.png` and `S-ext-02-flank-wide.png` (T1-ARCH capture) show the predicted result: the outer_works curtain renders as a near-black silhouette from the ramp foot, with no stone detail readable at all. FIRST ATTEMPT (superseded): two lights flanking the gate at energy 1.8/range 18, calibrated by guess rather than by the castle's own numbers -- re-rendered and made NO visible difference, because the castle's equivalent fix is fourteen braziers (energy ~1.69, range ~10.2 each) PLUS four wide shadowless sky-fill omnis (energy 1.4-2.4, range 30-50) covering a 10m curtain, and two small-range point lights are not that system at any energy. The five entries below are a smaller version of the SAME two-part recipe sized to this wall (20m wide, 8m tall, `outer_z` = local z -12): four fire points spread across the curtain's own width so no stretch of wall is more than ~5m from one, plus one wide, weak, shadowless sky-fill light standing off the approach the way the castle's own `sky_fill` entries do, so the wall does not read as pure orange with nothing else in it. VERIFIED PARTIAL by that pass's own report: the gate face (`S-ext-01`) came back lit; `S-ext-02`, a wide stand looking at the PERPENDICULAR west flank, was still mostly dark because all five of these sit on the south face only and none of them reach a `-x`/`+x` wall at all. A second independent judge pass, reading nothing either T1-ARCH report wrote, reproduced exactly that: 'from the flank it is the worst-reading structure in the world right now... an unlit warehouse dropped on the meadow'. The block below (`_comment_lights_flanks`) is the same recipe's own coverage gap closed on the two `-x`/`+x` walls it never reached, at `outer_works` (`z` 0) and `courtyard` (`z` 32) -- the only two chambers `scripts/world/stronghold.gd::EXTERIOR_CHAMBERS` dresses, because they are the only ones with a true, unroofed, meadow-facing perimeter.
_comment_lights_flanks: T1-ARCH-STRONGHOLD (2026-08-29). Same fire+sky-fill recipe as `_comment_lights_exterior` above, standing off the `-x`/`+x` flank walls instead of the `-z` gate face. `outer_works` is 20x24 (half-extent 10, wall_thickness 1.2, so the wall centreline sits at x=+-10.6 and its span runs z[-13.2,13.2]); `courtyard` is 22x28 centred at z=32 (wall centreline x=+-11.6, span z[16.8,47.2]). Fire stations spread every ~9-10m along each flank the same density the gate face uses (~5m clearance per station over a shorter wall); one sky-fill per flank, further out and high, mirroring the gate's own counterweight. `x` stands roughly 2m proud of the wall face -- close enough that the flank does not merely brighten by ambient bounce, the way the first (superseded) gate attempt did at range 18 from further off.
_comment_lights_flanks_budget: T1-HALL-REBUILD (2026-08-30), HALL_DESIGN_2026-08-30.md §7. The block below was TWELVE fire points plus FOUR sky-fills, sized when the flanks were the only lit exterior in the game and the wall values were a stop and a half darker than they are now. Two things changed under it: T1-HALL-BUILD raised the stone ladder (`site.stone_light`, the kit retints) so a flank no longer needs a fire every 9m to be legible at all, and the design's own measured budget caps the merged Hall at 18 exterior omnis, versus 21 on this branch's parent (4 gate fire + 1 gate sky-fill + 16 here). So: one fire PAIR per side spanning both yards (at the yards' own joint, z=16, where a 16m-range light reaches outer_works' back half AND courtyard's front half) plus one sky-fill per side moved to the same joint for the same reason -- 6 entries, not 16. The ten cut are paid for by §5's brighter walls, exactly as §7 says, and the ten omnis they free are what the causeway braziers and the yard fires in `hall_occupation` below are spent on. `stronghold.gd::_build_lights()` prints the live exterior count at build time and warns past 18, so this is a checked budget rather than a comment.

lights_flanks._comment: West flank fire 1/2 -- outer_works' own half.
West flank fire 2/2 -- the yards' joint, reaching courtyard's front half.
West flank sky-fill, one for both yards.
East flank fire 1/2 -- outer_works' own half.
East flank fire 2/2 -- the yards' joint.
East flank sky-fill, one for both yards.

_comment_lights_outer_works_ambient: T1-HALL-REBUILD (2026-08-30). The outer_works yard's own weak ambient omni (was `at [0,0], y 6, energy 0.35, range 18`) is RETIRED, not moved: `hall_occupation.braziers` now stands a real fire in this yard beside the garrison camp, and two more on the causeway kerbs a few metres outside the mouth. A yard lit by a fire the player can see burning is the whole point of the occupation layer; a colourless 0.35 ambient over the top of it is the thing that flattens it. Retiring it is also what brings the site to exactly the design's 18-omni ceiling (§7) with the causeway fires included.

lights._comment: T1-ARCH exterior fire 1/4, spread across the curtain's own width.

T1-ARCH sky fill -- the castle's own counterweight so the wall reads as fire-against-sky rather than as one warm flood. High and south of the wall, wide and weak, shadowless like every other light in this file.

_comment_hall_occupation: T1-HALL-REBUILD (2026-08-30), HALL_DESIGN_2026-08-30.md §6. THE LAYER THAT DIED WITH THE CASTLE. `landmark.gd` was the only caller of `stronghold_occupation.gd`, so retiring the detached castle (T1-HALL, `playground_world.gd`) took the game's entire garrison camp, brazier row and tether-lamp set out of the world along with it -- the merged Hall inherited the architecture and none of the occupation. This block is that vocabulary re-authored at the merged site, in THIS file's own local frame (x lateral, z depth, origin `site.at`, `yaw_deg` 0), not a second copy of `stronghold_occupation.json` (which still describes the retired castle's plinth-relative coordinates and is left alone as that building's history). Technique -- basket proportions, flame-without-stick, two-summed-sines flicker -- is ported from `stronghold_occupation.gd` per the design's own instruction to read it rather than extend it. Frames of reference per placement: `on_floor` sits a thing on the complex's own built floor (`_floor_y`, the yards); `on_causeway` sits it on the approach ramp's own sampled surface at that z; `on_ground` sits it on the real terrain (the boulders at the skirt foot). RESERVED-COLOUR DISCIPLINE: oxblood (#7a2430/#5a2a2e) and teal are Team Tether only; brass (#8a6f3a) appears only on Tether fittings; the Hall's own stone/timber palette uses none of the three.

hall_occupation._comment_braziers: SIX exterior fires, and six is the number the §7 light budget can afford: 4 gate fire + 1 gate sky-fill (`lights`) + 4 flank fire + 2 flank sky-fill (`lights_flanks`) + 1 courtyard ambient + these 6 = 18, the design's ceiling exactly. The design's own split was '3 causeway pairs + 2 gate braziers' with a separate yard ambient; this is the same six omnis spent as 2 causeway pairs plus a fire IN each yard, because the gate face already carries four fire lights that had no visible source at all (`gate_source` below gives two of them one, at zero light cost) and a yard with a fire burning in it reads as held far better than a yard with a colourless 0.35 ambient over it. Energies match the retired castle's own measured brazier range (~1.7-3.0).

braziers._comment: Causeway pair 2, west kerb -- two thirds of the way down the 40m climb; the pair spacing spreads the lit stretch over the whole causeway rather than clustering both pairs near the gate, which is what the first night frame showed.
The garrison camp's own fire, in the outer_works yard. Clear of the patrol trainer's stand at (-5,6) and of the gate/passage lane x[-4,4].
The inner bailey's fire, beside the relay hub. Clear of the courtyard trainer's stand at (-4,36).

hall_occupation._comment_gate_source: Two brazier BASKETS with no light of their own, standing at two of the four gate fire points `lights` already authors. The T1-ARCH gate recipe lit the curtain convincingly and put nothing in the frame that could be doing the lighting; these are that missing source, and they cost zero omnis because the light is already there.
hall_occupation._comment_causeway: The 40m climb, dressed. Kerbs are code boxes following the ramp's own self-derived slope (nothing here authors the rise; `site.ramp_run` is still the only authored number). `rail_pitch_m` spaces `Prop_WoodenFence_Single` along the kerb tops -- the board's timber approach. `banner_pairs` are the z stations for oxblood banners on stone piers; the piers are what a banner needs to hang from out on open ground.

causeway._comment_rail_pitch: RETIRED as an authored value. `stronghold.gd::_build_causeway_dressing` now derives the spacing from `Prop_WoodenFence_Single`'s own measured length at the fitted height (2.06m native x, scaled), because an authored pitch of 2.6 against a fitted panel of 2.7 overlapped every panel with its neighbour.

hall_occupation._comment_camp: The garrison camp in the gatehouse yard -- the board's Inner Yard stalls with a hostile owner. Same prop family the retired castle's checkpoint used (`generated_camp` tents/firewood, `kenney_survival` bedroll, `quaternius_fantasy` crates/barrel), so this is the Meadows' one camp vocabulary rather than a new one. Every entry sits on the yard's own built floor. THE CLEARANCES THIS LIST OBEYS, because a prop that blocks the route is worse than no prop: the gate/passage lane x[-4.5,4.5] stays empty end to end, the patrol trainer's stand (-5,6) keeps a 5m radius, and nothing sits closer than 1m to the yard walls at x=+-10.
hall_occupation._comment_camp_t1_hall_3: T1-HALL-3, 2026-08-30. The 18 entries after the Workbench dress the COURTYARD; everything before it is the outer-works garrison camp and is unchanged. JUDGE-5 ranked D2 second of sixteen: "the Warden arena is four untextured-looking tiled stone walls and a cobble floor -- no crates, no braziers, no banners, no apparatus, nothing that says anyone occupies it", and named occupation the FIRST of the three things separating these frames from the reference key art ("the reference stronghold is occupied; this one is empty"). Two things were true at once. The courtyard genuinely had one object in it (the relay hub) -- and that object sits at local z 27.4 while the H-07 stand looks SOUTH from the courtyard trainer, so the room's only piece of dressing was directly BEHIND the camera in every frame ever shot of it. Placement obeys the room's own two constraints rather than filling it: the courtyard is a trainer FIGHT room, so the fight floor (x[-5,5], z[24,42]) stays clear and every prop hugs a wall, and nothing sits in either doorway line at x~0. Same prop families the outer-works camp already uses (D24's one-camp-vocabulary rule) -- no new assets, no Meshy generation. The warden_arena itself is left deliberately bare per HALL_DESIGN sec8: that fight owns its floor.
hall_occupation._comment_relay_hub: Design §6.4: one `relay_apparatus.glb` in the inner bailey as the Hall's own distribution hub, fitted to ~4m because board 14 draws a squat machine that is never taller than a hall. Fenced by four short tether girders in the reserved oxblood, the same fitting language the interior trim already speaks. Sited east of the courtyard's centre line so it is clear of both the trainer's stand (-4,36) and the x=0 passage lane, and so the player meets it side-on walking through.
hall_occupation._comment_hoarding: The board's wall walk, delivered as EXTERIOR DRESSING and deliberately not as a walkable surface -- design §4's stated trade, because the two yard fights own their floors and a ledge halfway up a wall is a bug in a fight room. Timber deck on brackets outside the courtyard's west curtain, running 14m up to the mid-wall tower the massing prefab stands at (-11.1, 15.0). No colliders, by the same rule `_build_trim`'s girders already follow.
hall_occupation._comment_stairs: Design §4 tier 2: a flight against the courtyard's north-east interior corner, reading as the way up to the parapet without being one. Dressing, no collider -- same trade as the hoarding. Clear of the x=0 doorway lane and 14m from the courtyard trainer's stand. AUTHORED IN METRES rather than built from the kit's `Stairs_Exterior_*` modules: fitting a 2.0 x 1.20 x 2.08 stair block to a 4.6m rise scales its PLAN 3.8x too, and the first render had the flight driving straight through the courtyard's east wall and out the far side. `_fit_to_height` is right for a machine that only has to be a certain height and wrong for anything whose footprint matters.
hall_occupation._comment_grounding: The 'fits the Meadows, not floating' half of the acceptance list. Buttress pilasters down the east skirt face (the one that shows tall -- the west is half-buried in the shoulder the design sited the Hall against) plus half-buried nature-pack boulders at the skirt foot, wearing the same granite the Warrens' own cave stone does. Boulders sample the REAL terrain, so they follow whatever the ground under the skirt actually does rather than a straight authored line.

grounding._comment_skirt_face: How far DOWN the skirt's own facing skin runs from the floor line. The skirt is 18m deep but only its top few metres ever clear the ground (floor sits ~6m above the meadow here), so 8m covers every visible face with margin and buries the rest rather than skinning 18m of underground slab.

_comment_machine: PLACEHOLDER MASSING, AND IT MUST NOT BE MISTAKEN FOR THE ASSET. The Tether Machine has an owner-supplied board (docs/art/reference/15_Legendary_Tether_Machine.png, 2026-08-11) and is one of the three hero objects D24 reserves a Meshy generation for. The agent that built this route had no Meshy access, so what stands here is primitives plus the Tether materials, sized to the board's own ~15m scale bar, and the seam is left deliberately obvious: `placeholder: true` below, a name of `TetherMachinePlaceholder` in the scene tree, and no attempt at the board's surfacing. Replacing it is a one-object swap into `machine.model` -- the chamber, the lighting and the markers around it are all real and are what this item actually delivered. AND THE STANDING WARNING FROM THE BACKLOG: the board draws a legendary bound inside the containment ring because that is what the machine DOES to legendaries. The board licenses the MACHINE, never its occupant. Sec20/D23 forbid a new creature mesh at any credit balance, so the bound creature is an existing roster body or VFX placed by R8.4 -- there is no creature in this block and none may be added to it.

machine._scale_note: 15m against the board's own 0-20m bar. base_radius/ring_radius are read off the same board's plan proportions (the containment ring is a little under half the total height across), not invented -- but they are TUNABLE and will be replaced wholesale by the real mesh's own extents.
machine._comment_seam_closed: SEAM CLOSED 2026-08-16. The owner authorised the generation and the key came from the Ralph art-lane Routine. Meshy multi-image-to-3D, refine tier, from four crops of board 15 cut by tools/art_pipeline/crop_prop_views.py -- and the front and side crops had the BOUND LEGENDARY LIFTED OUT of them first, because D24 licenses the machine and not its prisoner and image-to-3D follows its pictures rather than its negative prompt. `height` below is still the authority: stronghold.gd fits the mesh to it by its own visual bounds. The primitive massing under `base_radius`/`ring_radius`/`core_radius` is kept as the fallback the code still takes when `model` is empty or missing, and as the record of what the chamber was built around.

_comment_recovery: SG38's recovery opportunity, and Sec8 puts it in the Tether Chamber Approach -- past the elite, before the Warden. It is `scripts/build/creature_bed.gd`, the SAME object R4.8 already ships as a buildable, placed here instead of built by the player: `home_recovery.gd::rest` heals a party member fully (reviving a fainted one) and grants progression.gd's rest XP. Reusing it rather than inventing a stronghold-only heal is the whole point -- a player who has built a bed at home already knows exactly what this is.
_comment_gauntlet: SG38. Sec8 and Sec12 between them ask for a patrol trainer at the Outer Works, a courtyard fight, an elite before the Tether Chamber, and 2-4 battles across the five spaces. Three is what stands here, and the fourth fight in the building is the Warden himself (R8.3). Every one of them is an ORDINARY entry in data/config/trainers.json -- same table, same teams, same SC15 reward schema, same defeat flags, same encounter_director.begin_trainer_battle() -- carrying `placed_by: "stronghold"` so trainer_npc.gd's own placer skips them and this file's layout decides where they stand. That is the only reason a position appears here rather than in trainers.json: a room's coordinates belong to the room. Every offset is deliberately OFF the doorway-to-doorway line through its space: a trainer standing in the middle of the way through is a body the player has to walk around before they have even been challenged.
_comment_marks: Named spots later items ask for BY NAME instead of by coordinate, exactly the rule burrow_warrens.gd's markers keep. R8.3 needs somewhere to stand the Warden and somewhere to stop the player for his dialogue; SG40 needs the spot the reveal is delivered from; R8.4 needs the machine's own foot and the place the freed legendary appears. All five are here so none of those items has to hard-code a metre. `offset` is [lateral, depth] from that chamber's own centre.
